Description: Potential regular expression denial of service vulnerability in EmailValidator and URLValidator, allowing attackers to cause significant CPU consumption with crafted input strings.
Potential denial of service in intcomma template filter when processing very long strings without separators, leading to memory exhaustion.
Unintended leak of Proxy-Authorization header to destination servers when redirected from an HTTPS endpoint to an HTTP endpoint, exposing credentials.
NULL pointer dereference when loading PKCS7 certificates that could lead to denial of service. Affects certificate parsing in the X.509 module.
NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in PKCS12 parsing that could be exploited by a malicious certificate bundle to crash the application.
Denial of service vulnerability: uncontrolled resource consumption when processing a specially crafted image file with large dimensions, causing excessive memory allocation.
Buffer overflow in the _imagingcms module when processing malformed ICC profiles, potentially allowing arbitrary code execution on the server.
SQL injection vulnerability when using the Loader Criteria feature with user-controlled input in relationship loading options.
Arbitrary code execution via unsafe YAML deserialization when using yaml.load() without specifying SafeLoader, allowing instantiation of arbitrary Python objects.
Cross-site scripting vulnerability in xmlattr filter when attribute values contain user-controlled data with special characters that bypass the default escaping.
Remote code execution through package_index module when downloading packages from a compromised or malicious PyPI mirror via command injection in URL handling.
Request body not stripped after redirect from 303 status code, potentially leaking sensitive POST data to the redirected endpoint.
Cookie header leaked via cross-origin redirect when using the Authorization header, allowing session hijacking if redirected to an attacker-controlled domain.
Removal of e-Tugra root certificate from the trust store due to security concerns. Systems using the older version trust a compromised certificate authority.
Path traversal vulnerability in the debugger console when running in debug mode, allowing remote code execution if the debugger PIN is known or guessable.
Minor information disclosure through error messages when connecting to PostgreSQL with malformed connection strings, revealing partial connection parameters.
HTTP Request Smuggling vulnerability due to improper parsing of HTTP Transfer-Encoding headers, allowing bypassing of security controls in reverse proxy configurations.
Privilege escalation in the Celery worker when using the --uid/--gid flags with certain task configurations, running tasks with higher privileges than intended.
Information disclosure in debug logging: AWS credentials may be logged in debug-level messages when connection errors occur during credential refresh.
Terrapin attack: prefix truncation vulnerability in SSH protocol implementation (ChaCha20-Poly1305 and CBC-EtM ciphers), allowing integrity bypass of encrypted SSH traffic.
Potential buffer over-read when processing malformed .npy files with mismatched header dtype declarations. Limited to denial of service in specific loading scenarios.
Algorithm confusion vulnerability allowing JWT signature bypass when the server accepts multiple algorithms. An attacker can forge tokens using HMAC with a leaked public RSA key.
LDAP injection vulnerability when user-controlled input is used in search filters without proper escaping, allowing authentication bypass or data exfiltration.
